title: We have Always Lived in the Castle

vibeProfile.oneLine: Two sisters live shunned in a grand house, and one of them tells you why.

summary: Eighteen-year-old Merricat lives in a grand, decaying house with her gentle sister Constance and their ailing uncle, shunned by a village that believes Constance poisoned the rest of the family years ago. Narrated in Merricat's strange, enchanting, faintly sinister voice, Shirley Jackson's final novel is a small masterpiece of unease, a study of outsiderhood, cruelty and fierce sisterly love that never quite tips into the horror it always seems about to become. Odd, funny and deeply disquieting.
whyReadIt: Shirley Jackson's eerie, enchanting last novel, narrated by one of fiction's strangest voices. Cosy and sinister at once.

funFacts.text: It was Jackson's last completed novel, published three years before her death.
